prompts.V39: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a realistic dark architectural production concept storyboard for a first-person 2D horror game, four equal numbered panels 01–04 in a 2 by 2 grid, landscape sheet. The setting is a fully enclosed internal maintenance passage in an old dense Chinese residential tower adapted for coercive confinement. This is M1, an internal switchback passage between 44F and 45F, not an outdoor catwalk and not seven floors. Enclose it with a low continuous roof, stained interior walls, pipes and a continuous handrail, with no open sky, no exterior facade or free-standing balcony. Panel 01: first-person hand beside the lower management door and its closed latch, narrow enclosed steps rising ahead. Panel 02: seven small sealed observation windows aligned along an internal wall, through the same continuous handrail; count exactly seven windows, none are doors. The interiors are obscured, four empty compartments and three motionless indistinct distant seated forms, not active ghosts. Panel 03: one selected sealed frosted observation window with a motionless distant seated silhouette behind glass, no facial features, injuries or graphic details, hand remains outside the glass and cannot enter. Panel 04: upper enclosed landing and door after the windows, rising only to 45F, same pipe and handrail continuity. Readable physically plausible architecture, restrained steel green, gray, dull amber practical light; original textures and spatial design rather than a collage of other games. Only text is panel numbers 01 02 03 04; no titles, no UI, no subtitles, no other writing, no gore, no weapons. This is a reference sheet not finished game art.
prompts.REF-LIFT: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a physically plausible realistic horror architectural reference sheet, four numbered panels 01–04 in a 2 by 2 grid, landscape. First-person views inside old Chinese iron scissor-gate freight elevators, narrow steel cage, continuously visible closed mechanical latch and metal threshold, no weapons, no injured people, no monsters. Panel 01 L1: actual iron inner gate remains closed and latched; brushed steel side panel reflects the same gate but its reflection is slightly open, an impossible subtle discrepancy; the actual door and its latch remain crisp and authoritative. Panel 02 L1: enclosed 30F maintenance landing, a small locally stored removable tread plate set in its matching floor recess with two fastening clips, inspection box and activation lever; same elevator remains behind. This platform is not 31F and no direct jump upstairs. Panel 03 L2: inside a different cold-store elevator; a warm false arrival lamp glows beyond a CLOSED iron gate, behind gate is a sealed metal wall without any landing or floor outside, inside a visibly empty cloth delivery bag hangs on wall. Physical latch stays locked. Panel 04 L2: true landing, same closed scissor gate, continuous solid exterior landing flush with cabin threshold, two clearly aligned engraved level marks and an unlettered physical floor plaque; the empty delivery bag remains inside. Material contrast makes false wall vs real solid platform unmistakable without color alone. All surroundings are internal shaft or enclosed landings, no open street or sky, subtle red mist through distant cracks only. Dim practical lamps but readable objects, gray oxidized steel and teal walls with amber lamps. Only text is 01 02 03 04. No automatic-opening representation, no falls, no human body in bag, no new room, no caption text or watermarks. Architectural production reference not finished artwork.
prompts.REF-U4: Use case: stylized-concept. A four-panel first-person psychological horror production storyboard, 2 by 2 landscape grid, numbered 01–04 only. Same enclosed 48F old residential passage in a dense Chinese tower in all panels, same camera lens, facing the same doorway, NEVER mirror or flip geometry. Dry lime plaster, a chipped doorframe with the chip slanting toward a continuous metal handrail, one long and two short welding scars on the handrail beside an upright post, a cold condensation pipe turns down BEFORE the doorway into a low floor maintenance hatch. Repeated unlettered door plaques are background only. Panel 01 before crossing: a first-person hand has just tied a SINGLE rough scrap-cloth knot underneath the weld scars, its longer torn end hangs down. A narrow impossible extra shadow lies just INSIDE the doorway, while chip, handrail, pipe and hatch remain readable. Panel 02 after a forward crossing: exactly the same original composition with exactly the same chip, weld marks, single cloth knot and hanging torn edge at same positions, hand has stopped beside the cloth; subtle darker internal doorway but no new corridor or visible entity. Panel 03: detail crop of the unchanged chipped frame and weld scars and single knot, cloth remains local; no double knot, no new clue and no letters. Panel 04: same passage now with the low floor hatch manually raised on a visible mechanical support, a fixed safe top step below and pipe entering below; haunted original doorway still stands open with narrow inner shadow, NOT cleared or magically transformed. Passage back toward elevator remains available; no falling through floor, no portal, no new ghost, no explanation of identity. Muted lime gray, steel green, soft amber practical lamps, dry plaster vs wet cold pipe, legible creepy spatial repetition. No sky, no UI, no written clues, no captions other than numbers, no gore. Concept only, final landmark design must follow original production spec.
prompts.REF-MECHANISM: Use case: stylized-concept. Realistic production concept sheet of existing mechanical puzzle props for a first-person Chinese dense-tower horror game, four equal numbered close-up panels in 2 by 2 landscape grid. No people except cropped hands, no gore or weapons. Panel 01: fixed inspection lamp on a sliding workshop bracket with exactly THREE detent positions, slotted mounting rail, a narrow-mouth metal shade seated flush on two clips, independent hinged light baffle; absolutely not a handheld flashlight. Cast a narrow task light onto a fixed bolt seat and a movable bolt shoulder bearing two separate engraved alignment marks, mechanically fixed to their respective objects. Panel 02: closer view of the same sliding bridge bolt, the fixed-seat mark and movable-shoulder mark aligned into one line, exposed locking hole and a separate manual lever that still has to be pulled; do not imply light automatically opens bridge. Panel 03: exactly THREE slim transparent water-level chambers in a closed six-unit counterweight circuit with three equal segmented scales; initial water volumes clearly left THREE units, center ZERO, right THREE; two transfer valve paths feed center from left/right, no faucet, no outside source. Panel 04: separate low maintenance bay beneath that water mechanism; fixed access ladder to left, spirit level bubble centered, manual nonreturn locking bolt beside a hinged movable tread and structural stop; show locking operation is separate from adjusting water. Metal and stained tile realistic measured proportions, readable task lighting with gray, steel green and amber accents. Do not add extra valves that imply new game controls. Only text is panel numbers 01 02 03 04, no words or answer labels. This sheet illustrates object/material relationships not final interactable diagrams.
